$comment: Prompt manifest for the environment props. This file is the source; the .glb files it
produces are cached in assets/meshy/ and committed, because they cost real credits and could
not be regenerated identically — Meshy is not deterministic. Re-running the generator skips
anything already cached, so a rebuild is free.
Meshy is used in PREVIEW mode only: it returns geometry with no materials and no textures,
which is exactly what is wanted. Refine would add a 1-2 MB texture per prop, blowing the web
download budget and clashing with the flat-shaded look. Colour is assigned afterwards in
tools/blender/props.py from the game's own palette, so the whole world stays coherent and a
finished prop lands at 30-50 KB instead of megabytes.
The subjects are the props the jungle world actually places (packages/core/src/world
/jungle.ts), not a generic set. Variant counts are where they are because repetition is what
makes a world look cheap — four mediocre rocks beat one excellent rock placed two hundred
style: stylized low-poly game asset, flat shaded, chunky simplified forms, soft rounded edges, minimal surface detail, no text, no logos, single centered object, neutral even lighting, no baked shadows, no ground plane, no base, no pedestal
negative: photorealistic, hyperrealistic, high detail, noisy displacement, baked shadows, ambient occlusion, ground plane, base, pedestal, text, watermark, multiple objects, scene, diorama, character, creature, human
